glm.feedback:
- Category: test
- Severity: high
- File: shared/tests/test_r2_worktree_capability_integration.py (test_campaign_level_tree_op_does_not_touch_either_sibling, ~line 60)
- Finding: The spec's Test strategy explicitly requires "a campaign-level `git clean -xfd`/`git add -A` does not touch either sibling." The test never invokes `git clean` or `git add -A` at all — it writes marker files into the worktrees, writes a `status.json` into the main tree, and then asserts the markers still exist. Every assertion is trivially true of an untouched filesystem; the test would pass even if campaign-level tree operations destroyed both siblings, because no such operation is ever executed. (This matters: `git clean -xfd` in the main tree can plausibly reach ignored content under `.worktrees/`, which is exactly the risk the spec asked to be proven safe.)
- Suggestion: Actually run `git -C <main> clean -xfd` (and/or `git add -A`) inside the test before asserting the sibling markers survive; assert the exit code and the post-state of both worktrees. If `git clean` does remove them, that is a real finding the capability needs to address (e.g. gitignore semantics or explicit exclusion), not a test to weaken.

- Category: test
- Severity: medium
- File: shared/tests/test_r2_worktree_capability_integration.py (test_a_simulated_lock_failure_during_a_touch_is_confirmed_non_fatal)
- Finding: This test is tautological: it wraps a call in `try/except` and sets a flag in the handler, then asserts the flag. Any exception (or none) passes; it does not exercise any runner behavior, because the "runner" is a markdown contract with no executable warn-and-continue code. The spec's test-strategy line "a simulated lock failure during a touch is confirmed non-fatal to the runner's own build" is only nominally covered — the actual non-fatality lives in prose in `sub-iterate-runner.md`, which no test can validate. A broken implementation (e.g. CLI exiting non-zero on success, or a crash rather than clean exit 1) would still pass this test.
- Suggestion: At minimum, assert the specific failure mode the contract depends on: the CLI exits 1 with a parseable block payload (not a traceback / not exit>1 signals) on a simulated failure, e.g. run `check_unit_lease.py` via subprocess with a missing state file and assert `returncode == 1` and valid JSON on stdout. Rename or drop the try/except tautology.

- Category: bug
- Severity: medium
- File: shared/scripts/lib/unit_lease.py, touch_unit_lease (~line 150, `with file_lock(...)`)
- Finding: `file_lock(..., timeout_seconds=30)` can raise `LockTimeout`, which is not a `UnitLeaseError`. `check_unit_lease.py` only catches `UnitLeaseError`, so a contended lock (>30s, plausible when N runners serialize on one `loop.lock` plus the orchestrator's own writes) produces an unhandled traceback instead of the documented "exit 1, could not touch, JSON payload" contract. The runner's warn-and-continue reading of "non-zero exit" happens to still hold, but the CLI's own documented exit-1-with-JSON behavior is violated and callers parsing stdout JSON will crash on the traceback text.
- Suggestion: Either catch `LockTimeout` in `touch_unit_lease` and re-raise as `UnitLeaseError("could not acquire loop.lock: ...")`, or add `LockTimeout` to the CLI's except clause so it emits the standard block payload and exits 1.

- Category: spec
- Severity: medium
- File: plugins/shipwright-iterate/agents/sub-iterate-runner.md (touch snippet, `--worktree "{campaign_worktree}"`)
- Finding: The runner's lease touch records `worktree={campaign_worktree}` in the unit's own row, but `check_unit_lease.py`'s own `--worktree` help and the spec's lease-field list say this field is the unit's own worktree path. It is only accidentally correct pre-flip (the unit "lives" in the shared campaign worktree). Post-flip, the spec's claim that these brief parameters are "reused unchanged at R5a" means the row's `worktree` field would permanently record the *campaign* worktree, not the per-unit worktree — precisely the stored-path value the security-hardening section says destructive callers must not trust, and which R4's reconcile/cleanup would read back. The doc's stated reuse-unchanged property hides a wrong value.
- Suggestion: Pass the runner's own `{project_root}` (pre-flip: campaign worktree; post-flip: per-unit worktree) as `--worktree`, or explicitly document in `campaign-worktree.md` that the row's `worktree` field is campaign-worktree-valued until R4 mints it, so a future cleanup never reads it as the per-unit path.

- Category: test
- Severity: low
- File: shared/tests/test_r2_worktree_capability_integration.py (test_two_sibling_per_unit_worktrees_are_independently_isolated)
- Finding: This test creates worktrees via raw `git worktree add` and only exercises the guard, not `setup_unit_worktree.py`. The sibling-isolation behavior of the actual wrapper (which is what production will call) is covered elsewhere, but the integration test named for the spec's "two per-unit worktrees created concurrently at sibling paths" AC never uses the wrapper nor exercises concurrency of creation — it's a sequential guard test duplicating `test_campaign_unit_worktree.py`. The "created concurrently" aspect of the AC is untested anywhere.
- Suggestion: Either create the two siblings through `setup_unit_worktree.py` (two subprocess calls, ideally interleaved) in this integration test, or note the concurrency-creation gap; at minimum invoke the wrapper so the AC's "created" verb matches the tested path.

- Category: edge-case
- Severity: low
- File: shared/scripts/lib/unit_lease.py, `_find_unit`
- Finding: The case-folded fallback can silently touch the wrong row if two units differ only by case (e.g. `r2` and `R2`), and the exact-match pass runs first so the folded pass only fires on a miss — but a folded match then writes lease fields onto a row whose canonical id differs from the CLI's `--unit-id`, with no warning. `is_unit_ready`'s convention is read-only; a write via folded match is a new hazard.
- Suggestion: Restrict the folded fallback to a read-only confirmation or emit a warning when the folded id differs from the row's exact id; or drop the fallback entirely since the runner receives `sub_iterate_id` verbatim.

Overall assessment: ship-with-fixes — the capability modules are solid and well-tested, but the headline integration test for campaign-level `git clean` isolation doesn't actually run the operation it claims to prove, the lock-timeout path breaks the CLI's documented error contract, and the runner brief writes the campaign worktree into the per-unit `worktree` lease field.

SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

openai.feedback:
- Category: spec  
  Severity: high  
  File: plugins/shipwright-iterate/agents/sub-iterate-runner.md:26  
  Finding: The new `campaign_worktree` and `state_path` parameters are only documented as runner inputs; no producer/call site populating them is included in the diff. Consequently, real campaign briefs will omit both values and the runner will skip all required liveness touches.  
  Suggestion: Update the campaign runner-brief construction to supply the campaign worktree path and its absolute `.shipwright/loop_state.json` path for every campaign sub-iterate.

- Category: bug  
  Severity: medium  
  File: plugins/shipwright-iterate/agents/sub-iterate-runner.md:48  
  Finding: The per-unit lease touch records `--worktree "{campaign_worktree}"`. Once R5a repoints `{project_root}` to the per-unit checkout, this will still persist the shared campaign worktree on every unit row, rather than the unit’s actual worktree. That breaks the per-unit lease/worktree identity required for retries and cleanup.  
  Suggestion: Pass the runner’s own worktree (`{project_root}` after the flip) to `--worktree`; retain `--campaign-worktree` solely for locating and validating the shared state file.

- Category: edge-case  
  Severity: medium  
  File: shared/scripts/lib/campaign_unit_worktree.py:156  
  Finding: The path-length gate checks the administrative directory path but not files Git creates within it, such as `.git/worktrees/<name>/gitdir`. A path whose admin directory is within 260 characters can still fail during `git worktree add` when that child path exceeds the Windows limit.  
  Suggestion: Include the longest administrative child path Git must create (at least `admin_path / "gitdir"`) in the maximum-length calculation and add a boundary test.

- Category: test  
  Severity: medium  
  File: shared/tests/test_r2_worktree_capability_integration.py:151  
  Finding: The “simulated lock failure” test only catches a missing-unit exception from `touch_unit_lease`; it neither invokes the runner’s touch commands nor simulates a campaign-session-lock failure. It would pass even if runner-side failures terminated the build, so it does not validate the required warn-and-continue behavior.  
  Suggestion: Exercise the runner-facing command path with both lease and session-lock touch failures, then assert the subsequent build/finalization action still runs.

- Category: test  
  Severity: low  
  File: shared/tests/test_r2_worktree_capability_integration.py:59  
  Finding: The claimed campaign-level `git clean -xfd` / `git add -A` isolation test only writes `status.json`; it never executes either Git operation. It therefore does not cover the explicit integration acceptance criterion.  
  Suggestion: Run the actual commands in the campaign worktree and verify both sibling worktree markers remain unchanged.

Overall assessment: ship-with-fixes. The lease capability is largely present, but missing brief wiring prevents its required liveness behavior from running, and the persisted worktree path is wrong after the intended R5a transition.

SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
